scheduleNotes.message: Onboarding (weeks 1–3): a lecture every session, plus two assignments running in parallel — the ticket hunt (broad reconnaissance, due 9/16) and gradebook column groups (one deep vertical slice, due 9/24). Come to Thu 9/10 with a local dev environment running.
Project bids due Thu 9/17. Teams announced Thu 9/24.

Studio phase begins. Weekly rhythm: Mon standup + clinic · Wed tech talk or student presentations · Thu team work session, game day or demo day. Students merge to staging behind course feature flags; the instructor promotes to production periodically.

Async week, instructor at OOPSLA/ISSTA. The individual objective for this fortnight is an investigation in your team's area, not a shipped change: nothing needs to merge while nobody is watching Sentry. Artifact due Tue 10/13.
Feature freeze Mon 11/23. Weeks 13–14 are hardening, documentation and ops playbooks for the January 2027 handoff.

assignments.title: The Ticket Hunt
assignments.notes: File 2 tickets, triage 2 existing items. Builds the cs4535-first-ticket pool published Sep 17.

assignments.title: Project Bids
assignments.notes: Ranked preferences across the project slate

assignments.title: Reading Bid
assignments.notes: Rank your top three readings from the list, one sentence each on why, plus the artifact you think you could bring. Off-list proposals allowed; approved or rejected Sep 28.

assignments.title: Onboarding: Gradebook Column Groups
assignments.notes: Design bake-off — everyone implements first-class gradebook column groups independently, as a draft PR that never merges. Banded: Pass/Credit/Distinction.

assignments.title: Declare Your Target Band
assignments.notes: Changeable in either direction through Thu 12/3, no penalty.

assignments.title: Drill Zero — Async Triage Log (pass/fail)
assignments.notes: Pass/fail. A credible triage log passes even if you never fixed it — saying what you ruled out and how is the point.

assignments.title: Async Sprint: Focused Learning + Team Sync (Oct 2–13)
assignments.notes: Process requirements: cadence, standup #1 in Discord Mon 10/5 and standup #2 in the room Wed 10/14, two team sync points with rotating written summaries. The individual objective is one investigation in your team's area, in one of five shapes (trace, spike, reproduction, research, practice); the artifact is a page plus a link, committed to the team repo.

assignments.title: Checkpoint 1
assignments.notes: Written per-student judgment: on track for your declared band — yes or no, and why.

assignments.title: First Implementation Ticket
assignments.notes: Assigned at Demo Day 1, in your team's project area, and drawn from what your async-sprint spike turned up. Merged to staging by Thu 10/29 and verified in your team's demo class; a course feature flag only if the change is user-visible and unfinished. Demoed at Demo Day 2.

assignments.title: Checkpoint 2
assignments.notes: Written per-student judgment: on track for your declared band — yes or no, and why.

assignments.title: Feature Freeze — flags set, ops playbooks drafted
Code Review (continuous)
assignments.notes: Continuous, from GitHub history; nothing to submit. Pass: at least 6 substantive reviews, at least 2 outside your project area, and every comment on your own PRs answered within 48h. Credit: 3 reviews where your comment changed the code. Distinction: an accepted entry on the checklist.

assignments.title: Reading Presentation (pairs)
assignments.notes: Two students co-present one reading, two readings per session; co-presenter from outside your project team. Readings come from a fixed 13-item list, tagged by cross-project function. Sessions Oct 21 / Oct 28 / Dec 2; if enrollment runs past twelve, either a fourth session or one group of three, decided Sep 24 once bids are in.

assignments.title: Game Day Postmortems (3)
assignments.notes: One postmortem per game day, due within 48h of each

assignments.title: Checkpoint 3
assignments.notes: Written per-student judgment: on track for your declared band — yes or no, and why.

assignments.title: Learning Summary Report
assignments.notes: State the band you are applying for and justify it against the published criteria, linking each requirement to its artifact. Graded as verification of a claim.

metadata.description: A professional practicum capstone. A small cohort works on Pawtograder, a production platform with 1,500+ weekly active users, practicing the full software development lifecycle from design through operations.
